claims.head: Skinner’s hold on the Senators won’t last
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Skinner has been a wall against the Senators, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Senators finally get to him.

claims.head: Tilted ice, toward the Jets’ net
claims.body: The Senators have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Jets near the bottom. Expect the Senators to spend more of the night in the Jets’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

story.head: The Jets come in hot
paras: The Jets have won six straight, and they’re rolling. The Senators have won two in a row. Going in, the Sens are second in the Atlantic (tied for sixth in the NHL) and the Jets fifth in the Central (tied for 15th).
The Senators’ record (.667) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.577), largely because they’re 6-2 in one-goal games. The Jets’ record (.548) is about what their chances are worth.

The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd), play slow, tight games (3rd lowest) and get into more chippy games than almost anyone (3rd). As for the Jets, they ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd) and create chances on the penalty kill (3rd). They also get their shots through better than almost anyone (3rd), and their knack for getting shots through meets a team that blocks a lot. Expect a chippy, heavy game.

Tim Stützle (11 G / 14 A / 25 P in 21 GP) leads the Senators in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Winnipeg. Drake Batherson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 21 GP) is next in line. Kyle Connor (17 G / 9 A / 26 P in 21 GP) is tied for the Jets’ scoring lead, with nine points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against Ottawa. Mark Scheifele (7 G / 19 A / 26 P in 21 GP) shares it, with twelve points in his last five games.

Linus Ullmark (9-1-0 / .939 SV% in 10 GS) has been a rock in net for Ottawa and is expected to start. Stuart Skinner (7-4-3 / .880 SV% in 15 GS) is expected to go for Winnipeg. Skinner has a .931 save percentage in five starts against the Senators, well above his usual .895. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
The Senators usually control more of the chances than the Jets do.

The Jets are newly without Dylan DeMelo and Isak Rosén, and have been without Elias Salomonsson since Nov 3.
